facts.text: PWS Plasma Wave Dipole Antenna was deployed at Interstellar Space (Beyond Heliopause) during Voyager Interstellar Mission in 1977.
facts.source: Gurnett et al. (Science 2013) / University of Iowa

facts.text: Two 10-meter beryllium-copper boom antennas deployed in a 90-degree V-configuration, sensing electric field fluctuations and electron plasma oscillations from 10 Hz to 56 kHz.
facts.source: Gurnett et al. (Science 2013) / University of Iowa

facts.text: Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the lunar environment.
Provided the definitive scientific proof that Voyager entered interstellar space when it detected a forty-fold increase in electron plasma density outside the heliosphere.
A permanent human and robotic monument celebrating space exploration on the Moon.

scenes.kids: I am PWS Plasma Wave Dipole Antenna. I arrived here at Interstellar Space (Beyond Heliopause) in 1977.
scenes.explorer: PWS Plasma Wave Dipole Antenna, Voyager Interstellar Mission: deployed at Interstellar Space (Beyond Heliopause) in 1977.

scenes.kids: Take a look at how I was built. Every part of me had a special purpose.
scenes.explorer: Two 10-meter beryllium-copper boom antennas deployed in a 90-degree V-configuration, sensing electric field fluctuations and electron plasma oscillations from 10 Hz to 56 kHz.

scenes.kids: Out here, there is no air or weather like on Earth, so I had to work smoothly in the cold.
scenes.explorer: Designed to withstand radiation, cosmic dust, and extreme temperature swings without failing.
